overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an August 10 notice without the physical meeting location and by approving June 8 minutes late, but found no intentional violation and ordered only future compliance.

allegations.summary: Notice for the August 10 meeting, which offered in-person attendance, did not state the physical meeting location.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Board was not required to provide both in-person and remote access to its August 10 meeting, because the meeting notice did identify an in-person option, the notice needed to provide enough detail to reasonably inform the public of the physical location of the meeting.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the June 8 meeting were not reviewed and approved within the timeframe allowed by the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Because the September 14 meeting was more than three meetings and 30 days past the June 8 meeting, we find that the June 8 meeting minutes were not timely approved, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the untimely approval of the June 8 minutes was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not find the violation here to be intentional.

remedy: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
